title: A Stretched Cosine Wave
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the amplitude and period of $y=\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$, explaining why this wave takes longer than the standard cosine to repeat.

steps.title: Read Off the Coefficients
steps.explanation: The argument $x/2$ means $B=1/2$, and nothing scales the output vertically.
steps.why: Recognizing $B$ inside the argument is the key step for period questions.

steps.title: Confirm the Amplitude
steps.explanation: Output values still reach exactly $\pm 1$, so the amplitude remains one.
steps.why: Horizontal stretching does not alter vertical extent.

steps.title: Compute the Stretched Period
steps.explanation: Dividing by the half doubles the base period, so the wave needs $4\pi$ to finish one cycle.
steps.why: A coefficient below one in the argument stretches the graph horizontally.
